questions.key_step: Series expansion to order x^3 for k, then the mirror-image/parallel-tangent idea for the distance between inverse curves.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (precise Taylor cancellation, inverse-curve symmetry) with option checks and light arithmetic.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2024-P2-Q3 (L1) + 2026-P2-Q2 (L2); two ideas linked puts it at 3

questions.key_step: Pair x with its reflection so that [t]+[-t]=-1 applies, twice for the cosine part.
questions.justification: Greatest-integer integrals via King property need the non-integer almost-everywhere argument; two applications, options to check.

questions.key_step: Partial fractions, constant from f(2), slopes at the common point, angle formula.
questions.justification: Routine multi-step chain without insight; options to confirm.

questions.key_step: Factor n^6-k^6+n^2k^2(n^2-k^2)=(n^2-k^2)(n^2+k^2)^2 to get a Riemann sum, then x=sin t, tan t.
questions.justification: The hidden factorisation is the one non-routine step; the integral that follows is standard.

questions.key_step: Find the common tangent of C1 and a parabola: intercept condition -3m^2/8 and the point x1=1/sqrt2.
questions.justification: Four statements, f from a differential relation, then a common-tangent search whose root must be spotted; options allow verification of B.

questions.key_step: Second derivative of composites at 0: (f o g)''=f''(g)g'^2+f'(g)g'' for three composites.
questions.justification: Three similar long-chain computations where one slip changes the verdict; each statement needs a real check.

questions.key_step: Divide by x^2 and u=x+1/x, then u=sec t, to get f=sqrt((x^2-x+1)/(x^2+x+1)); then root location of a cubic.
questions.justification: Unfamiliar integration trick (palindromic radicand) feeding a cubic root-location analysis with four statements.

questions.key_step: Point of L on the radical axis has equal tangent lengths, so it is the midpoint of T1T2 and the circle on T1T2 is orthogonal to the system.
questions.justification: Coaxial/radical-axis reasoning that students rarely meet in this form, several statements, a trapezoid area to finish.

questions.key_step: Spot the invariance of 1+2cos(2x-pi/3) under x->pi/3-x, the identity 1+sqrt3 tan(pi/3-x)=4/(1+sqrt3 tan x), then the cos-integral.
questions.justification: Three King-property integrals plus a combination, with an extra t=tan(theta/2) integral; long and error-prone.

questions.key_step: Wallis formula for three items and the reduction T4+T2=1/3 for tan^4.
questions.justification: Four short standard evaluations with elimination possible.

questions.key_step: Reflection formula for the image, then d^2=r1^2+r2^2 for orthogonal circles.
questions.justification: Four independent routine items, each a short chain.

questions.key_step: From the moments int f=0 and int x f=0 argue that (x-c)f cannot keep one sign, hence at least two roots; show 2 is attained.
questions.justification: Non-routine sign-change/orthogonality argument plus a construction; no options to check.

questions.key_step: Integrate x^{k-1}f_{n+1} by parts to get the recursion with (n-k), and use k=1 repeatedly.
questions.justification: Unfamiliar recursion on an operator sequence, several stages, no options.

questions.key_step: f(1)=f(4) so c is the critical point x=2, and M,m from endpoints and f(2).
questions.justification: Single familiar move, a table of three values.

questions.key_step: f'>=0 for all x, with the degenerate case a^2-1=0 treated separately, then count integers.
questions.justification: Routine chain with one trap (a=-1) and a clean discriminant condition.

questions.key_step: Corners at half-integers and a jump at x=1 give m=3; du/dv from derivatives on (1,2).
questions.justification: Routine casework with one easy-to-miss discontinuity; short second part.

questions.key_step: N/T = dy/dx makes the relation a separable ODE; solve and evaluate.
questions.justification: Standard definitions plus a one-line separable equation.
